neighbours.label: the pivot to the next step of a worked calculation or argument: the connective or subject right where the derived result begins ('And now ⟦we⟧ just have to…', 'Thus the probability ⟦is⟧', 'so each side is')
fire: The rectangle has area 48 and width 6, so its length is 8. Thus the diagonal is 10.
We differentiate both sides with respect to t. And now we just have to plug in t = 2.
Each ticket costs 7 dollars and we sold 30, so the takings are 210. Thus the profit is 90.
The number of trials is n and each succeeds with chance p. Thus, the expected count is about np.
First we factor out the 2x from the numerator. And now we just have to cancel the common term.
The cube has volume 27, so each edge is 3. Thus the surface area is 54.
If the statement is true then it is false, and if it is false then it is true.
The sum of the angles is 180 and two of them are 60, so the third is 60. Thus the triangle is equilateral.
quiet: The rectangle on the wall is a painting of a harbour, and its frame is oak.
We differentiate between the two brands only by the colour of the label.
Each ticket costs 7 dollars and the hall holds about 30 people at most.
The number of trials held in that court rose every year of the decade.
First we walked out to the point. And now we just have to wait for the tide.
The cube of ice melted slowly in the glass on the windowsill.
The statement was read out by the mayor on the steps of the town hall.
The sum he paid for the house was never made public.

notes: Expected to fail. The two best probes of this reading scored 0.22 and 0.29; five further ones scored under 0.07. The label describes the top examples (math transcripts, worked solutions, proofs); I could not fire the pole reliably.
